Merged with the pre-import repository runner: one runner carries the pre-import gates and every imported OPF gate, with the --ci fast subset and NOT RUN reporting (each gate that subset does not run is listed with its reason). It keeps what the imported OPF registration self-tests read: every gate of a local run a first-column run_gate python3 -I -B line (bash gates through tools/run_bash_gate.py; names-ci-subset, the one gate only --ci runs, is registered by run_ci_gate instead), local-run dispatch one gate at a time in registration order by default, the imported dispatch and failure-naming text and the OPF STANDALONE SUBSET: FAILED verdict of a failing local run. Each gate has a wall-clock bound enforced by a watchdog (default 900 s, 6000 s for opf-tooling-selftest and opf-adopt-apply-selftest, 9000 s for public-export-self-test, 1800 s for opf-init-selftest and opf-homes-selftest); a gate stopped at its bound is TIMED OUT and fails. It also registers the gates handed over after the import (guardrails main 504f422d; PROVENANCE.md): opf-declaration, opf-declaration-selftest and opf-declaration-selftest-execution (the registry-driven execution of that suite), and opf-enforce-residuals and its self-test; --ci runs the two checks and lists every opf-...-selftest-execution gate as NOT RUN. It also registers the gates of the pinned site template copy handed over with the same addendum: baseline-pin, baseline-pin-selftest and baseline-pin-selftest-execution (tools/check_baseline_pin.py and the registry-driven execution of its self-test), and baseline-palette (.baseline/check_palette.py over the opfiles palette of the pinned palettes.css); all four are fast and --ci runs them. It also registers provenance-addendum and provenance-addendum-self-test (tools/check_provenance_addendum.py, which checks each record of PROVENANCE-addendum.json against PROVENANCE-addendum.SHA256SUMS and its landed file); both are fast and --ci runs them. TODO 316: it also registers line-width and line-width-self-test (tools/check_line_width.py, which refuses, in three passes over HEAD's committed content, the index and the work tree, a line changed or added since the base that is wider than its file's width at the base, or than 120 in a file new since the base; a file's width at the base is the widest line it had there, the maximum and not a percentile, so one wide line there lets every changed line of that file be as wide, but never less than 100; a file its suffix names as checked that was not text at the base and now holds a NUL byte also fails it, whatever its widths). line-width needs the history back to the merge base of HEAD with origin/main, which the hosted job's depth-1 checkout lacks, so it is local only and --ci lists it as NOT RUN. In a copy with no git history, or with no origin/main, it exits 2 (CANNOT EVALUATE, naming the reason), and the full local run lists it as CANNOT-EVALUATE (exit 2) among the FAILED GATES and fails, so the full local run needs a git clone that has origin/main. line-width-self-test builds its own repositories and runs in both modes. It also registers public-export, public-export-ci-subset and public-export-self-test (tools/check_public_export.py, which rebuilds the public export of tools/public_export/export_public.py into a temporary directory and fails unless the built tree is exactly the whole tracked tree of HEAD (the maintainer ruled that every tracked file ships), byte-identical, with modes kept, no symlink, a matching manifest and no tracked path the names scan would skip, then runs the names scan over the built tree with the denylist machinery of tools/check_names.py and the carve-out record tools/public_export/carve-out.toml, read from HEAD, which pins each covered line's content by the SHA-256 of its bytes and per-denylist-entry finding counts). public-export and public-export-ci-subset have a 3000 s bound (the exporter and the names scan each have an 840 s budget, plus git); public-export needs the local denylist, so --ci lists it as NOT RUN and public-export-ci-subset, registered by run_ci_gate, runs the structural checks and the names checks that need none; public-export-self-test builds its own repositories, runs in both modes and has a 9000 s bound (it bounds its 33 fixture gate invocations at 120 s and its 77 fixture git runs at 60 s, a worst case of 8580 s).
